clue.text: Short and deceptively healthy hair taking seconds to train?

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
a weave is added artificial hair that makes a head of hair look fuller than it is

explanation.surface: A description of a hairstyle: a short cut with extensions that make it look thicker than it is.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing a fighter's 'seconds' are the corner assistants, so the definition pictures a boxer in training practising a dodging move.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducking and swaying is a boxer's evasive technique, drilled in training with the corner team watching.

clue.text: Fat-free bolognese does not require lengthy preparation

indicators.note: the letters of a second word are subtracted from the sauce's name, as if it can do without them
the sauce's letters are prepared, mixed up into a new order

parts.note: lengthy means long

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: a low-fat bolognese sauce is quick to make.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: BOLOGNESE holds the letters of LONG plus those of the answer, shuffled together by 'preparation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly overweight people are described as fat; the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: First strike a wild lunge before the bell

indicators.note: the A and the jumbled lunge come before the opening letter of strike
a wild lunge is out of control, so the word's letters are thrown into disorder
the first letter of strike is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer throws a wild first punch just before the bell rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First strike' looks like the opening blow of a fight, but it only gives S, placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus bell is rung in Catholic churches to call the faithful to that devotional prayer.

clue.text: Spent a quid on unlimited rice wine cocktail

parts.note: taken as written; quid is slang for a pound

indicators.note: the Japanese drink loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: mirin is a Japanese rice wine used in cooking

explanation.surface: Someone paid a pound for a cocktail made with rice wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' trims MIRIN to IRI, which joins A and QUID to be shuffled by 'Spent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum, lime and sugar mixed drink named after a Cuban town is a classic cocktail.

clue.text: Woefully gaunt bottom lost by weakling turned body-builder

indicators.note: a letter is lost from the strongman's name

parts.note: Charles Atlas, famous for advertisements about a 97-pound weakling who built up his muscles

indicators.note: the bottom, or last, letter of gaunt is taken

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a thin man who once was weak and became a body-builder, but lost his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Atlas sold body-building courses with the story of a weakling who got kicked sand in his face; removing the T from his name leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief, used to say something is regrettably so, as 'woefully' does.

clue.text: Make weak brew of tea? Never!

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture stirred up, so the letters of the words are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to make the tea too weak.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap someone's energy or strength is to make them weak; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Knee-trembler with less than wholeheartedly demure Max Clifford-type excited promiscuous nightclub singer

indicators.note: both words suggest wild, disordered behaviour, so all the pieces are mixed together
the knee trembles, so its letters shake about
the word demure loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: Max Clifford was a British publicist, a PR (public relations) man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid-style string of words about sex, publicists and nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is KNEE, DEMRE, PR and NIGHTCLUB, twenty letters in all. Bloggers criticised the clue as non-Ximenean, with stacked indicators and a nonsense surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Engelbert Humperdinck is the stage name of a British crooner famed for Release Me.

clue.text: See 7
Bird found in central Argentina and west of Uruguay

indicators.note: the central letter of Argentina is taken
in an across clue the west end of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird whose range lies in central Argentina and to the west of Uruguay.
explanation.definitionFit: The nandu is another name for the rhea, a large flightless South American bird.

clue.text: Island society of new and old money

parts.note: taken as written
the guinea was a British coin worth 21 shillings, out of use since 1813 but long used for pricing

explanation.surface: High society, a mix of the newly rich and those with inherited wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island north of Australia shared by Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

clue.text: Peruse volume mistakenly put on table

indicators.note: the letters are wrongly ordered and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone reads a book and then puts it down on the table by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out food at a meal is to place it on the table; the phrasal verb fits.

clue.text: The Alarm's live album still in circulation

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the record goes in, surrounded by the calming word

parts.note: to lull is to still or calm
LP, long-player, is an album record

explanation.surface: A review of a live album by the Welsh rock band The Alarm that is still on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alarm was a 1980s Welsh rock band, which makes 'live album' look like music talk; here the alarm is a summons rung by cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord pulled to ring a bell for a servant serves as a household means of raising the alarm.

clue.text: Home visitor — more than eleven letters!

definitions.text: Home visitor — more than eleven letters!

parts.words: Home visitor — more than eleven letters!
parts.note: the caller at your house who delivers mail has a heavy round carrying lots of letters; the answer itself also runs to eleven letters

explanation.definitionFit: An overworked mail carrier calls at homes and is carrying a great many letters.

clue.text: Rocking, real S.O.B. — like the Stones' frontman

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters about, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of the Rolling Stones' singer as a rocker and a real so-and-so.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick Jagger, the Rolling Stones' lead singer, is famous for his big lips.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare adjective means thick-lipped, and Mick Jagger's large lips are his trademark.

clue.text: An Orwellian conclusion to plot set in US college town

parts.note: an arbor, the American spelling of arbour, is a shady garden plot or bower

explanation.walkthrough: 'set in US' signals the American spelling of arbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann Arbor in Michigan is home to the University of Michigan, a classic American college town.

clue.text: Journalists' fees

definitions.meaning: sub-editors on a newspaper are called ...
membership fees or subscriptions are called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both sub-editors and subscriptions are shortened in everyday British use to the same word.

clue.text: Bass sound of Lou Reed's music

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: the name Lou is heard, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: the first name of the singer Lou Reed
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: The bass line of Lou Reed's songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lou Reed looks like one name, the Velvet Underground singer, but the clue splits it into a sound and a plant.

clue.text: Without Ray's lead or the backing of Matta and Mesens, Surrealism would have fallen into disorder

indicators.note: some letters are taken away from the art movement's name
the remaining letters fall into a new order
the lead, or first, letter of Ray's is taken
the backs of Matta and Mesens are their last letters

explanation.walkthrough: Man Ray, Roberto Matta and E.L.T. Mesens were Surrealist artists. Remove R, A and S from SURREALISM and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad or chaotic government brings disorder; the noun names that state of lawless confusion.

clue.text: Old fighter doctor brought round unexpectedly quits ringside

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O, set at the side

explanation.surface: At a boxing match, a veteran fighter is revived by a doctor and unexpectedly quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fighter' suggests a boxer, but it is a Second World War aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Mosquito was a wooden British fighter-bomber aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Nothing in helter-skelter luge run equates to tedium

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the jumbled letters

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A luge run down an ice track is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, dull stretch in a book or piece of music is called this, from French for length.

clue.text: Setback for Brazil meeting Sweden in knock-out

explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone with a blow is to knock them out; the verb and noun overlap in sense.

clue.text: One side of disc has middling hornpipe jig, which is hard stuff to take

indicators.note: one side of the word disc is its second half
a jig is a lively dance, so the letters jump about
the middle letters of hornpipe are taken

explanation.surface: One side of a record has a hornpipe and jig, which is hard to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc' halves into DI and SC; SC starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard stuff means strong spirits, and the German clear spirit is one example.

clue.text: A verse so unfathomable it could be Greek

indicators.note: something unfathomable can't be worked out, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem so obscure it might as well be in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's all Greek to me' suggests incomprehensible; here Greek just means foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something Greek, to a Briton, is foreign, from abroad across the sea.

clue.text: This beats, say, good Scotch, but — it has to be said — why?

parts.note: the word said aloud, which sounds like the letter Y

explanation.walkthrough: 'This beats' is a definition by function: the answer is something that beats eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool used for whipping or beating eggs is what 'this beats' describes.

clue.text: Disregard dregs of humour in appalling puns

clue.text: Tailoring features retro-cut uniform pattern

clue.text: Nice part of France

parts.note: reads like a pleasant region, but Nice is the city on the French Riviera

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like a mild adjective; capitalised, it is the Riviera city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera region on the Mediterranean contains the city of Nice.

clue.text: Retirement account is something worth having

explanation.surface: A pension account is valuable to have.

explanation.definitionFit: Anything valuable or useful that one owns counts as a valuable possession.

clue.text: Prosciutto starter and minestrone soup are never off the menu
